chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: A taped act reaches Wiesbaden; Lou Irwin gets him home for the Bill Robinson Story
summary: A woman recorded his act and sent it to Special Service headquarters; Lou Irwin then got him a part in the Bill Robinson picture and Bob Hope soon asked for him.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You know what this woman did? She took a tape just like you got there and recorded my act -- I'll never forget this as long as I live -- recorded my act and sent my act into Wiesbaden where the headquarters for the Special Service was and let the man over at headquarters hear it and that man from then on I was in the driver's seat. You understand? When he heard me entertain he must have contacted America and told America about me, 'cause as soon -- I don't get back right then, I'm there yet scruffing up money for my fare to come back to America. What got me back was Lou Irwin. Lou got a part for me to do in a picture, the Bill Robinson Story, I was number one on the dancing list for the Bill Robinson Story because I could sing, dance and talk and move and act, 'cause I'd been in everything. You understand?
So I get back here, leaving

Germany, I left Wiesbaden, Germany, and went by way of London to come to New York and I got back into New York, I wasn't here no time before Bob Hope was asking for me to go with the show. Now you know that was really moving, wasn't it?
